title: Nitra
capsule: The Principality of Nitra was a Slavic polity centered on the Nitra River valley in what is now western Slovakia, traditionally associated with Prince Pribina, who is recorded as having had a Christian church consecrated at Nitra by Archbishop Adalram of Salzburg around 828. The principality was conquered and absorbed into Great Moravia by Mojmír I around 833, who expelled Pribina and unified the Nitrian and Moravian territories. After Great Moravia collapsed under Magyar pressure around 906–907, the Nitra region passed into the nascent Hungarian realm, and the date range 898–911 in the Cliopatria dataset appears to reflect a brief period of attested separate identity at the end of Moravian fragmentation.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The historical existence of the principality before Mojmír's conquest is attested in Frankish chronicles, but the territorial extent — especially for the 898–911 window — is highly uncertain and primarily estimated from archaeological finds and later administrative boundaries.
